## An item written without a body reports a type-annotations-needed error for that body (E0284 TypeMustBeKnown at its root `ExprId(0)`)

`const A: u8;`, `static A: u8;`, `static mut C: u8;` and a free `fn f1();` inside `main` each get the user-facing error ("free constant/static item / free function without body"). They also get `InferenceDiagnostic::TypeMustBeKnown { at_point: ExprId(0), top_term: None, kind: E0284, .. }` for the body's root, which is `Expr::Missing`. It has no syntax, so blaze-diagnostics prints `blaze: type checking's TypeMustBeKnown { .. } .. which blaze cannot place`. In rustc a missing body is an error body: typeck is tainted and reports nothing more. Fix in hir-ty inference: a body whose root is `Expr::Missing` (or an `Expr::Missing` anywhere: its type is the error type, not a fresh variable) yields no ambiguity diagnostic. Related to 01379 (Sized of a trait method with no body), same family. Tests: blaze-diagnostics tests::items::ast_validation::{free_consts_without_bodies, free_statics_without_bodies, which_functions_need_a_body} (round15-test.log).

history.note: fixed by 01371 (hir-ty infer/expr.rs: Expr::Missing keeps the error type, no fresh var): free_consts_without_bodies, free_statics_without_bodies, which_functions_need_a_body pass in test-diag-1028.log.
